newsitem.title: QATAR: Egypt to cut Suez rates for Qatar LNG to Europe.
newsitem.headline: Egypt to cut Suez rates for Qatar LNG to Europe.

text.p: Egypt will sign a deal next week with Qatar offering liquefied natural gas shipments to Europe from the Gulf state concessional Suez Canal transit rates, officials said on Monday.
"The groundwork for the deal has already been prepared by visiting officials from the two countries," Egyptian ambassador to Doha Mohammad Minessey told reporters.
Qatar's Minister of Energy and Industry Abdullah bin Hamad al-Attiyah is due to fly to Cairo on Friday to sign the accord next week, the ambassador added.

Qatar energy ministry officials said Egypt had offered 35 percent rebate for Qatari LNG tankers transiting the canal, a measure which could make exports from Qatar more competitive in European markets which are dominated by natural gas imports from Russia, the North Sea and North Africa.
"This will serve as a good incentive for European consumers to source their LNG supplies from Qatar," said one official.
In May Qatar announced the sale of 420,000 tonnes (910,000 cubic metres) of LNG to Spain, which it will start shipping in cargoes of 31,500 tonnes for 13 months from next September.
Tiny Qatar, which controls the world's third largest gas reserve, is also discussing similar short-term, long-term and spot sales with other potential LNG customers in Europe.
"The canal tax rebate will apply to all sales because it is going to be a long-term deal between Qatar and Egypt", said the Egyptian ambassador.

During his visit Attiyah will be accompanied by a team of officials from Qatar Liquefied Gas Company (Qatargas), Qatar Fertiliser Company and Qatar Petrochemical Company to discuss the supply of fertilisers and petrochemical products to Egypt.

Egypt has expressed interest in buying one million tonnes of chemical fertilisers and "substantial amount" of ethylene dichloride and polymers from Qatar to set up a string of plastic and pharmaceutical projects, Minessey said.
